# LaTeXShot v1.0.0

- Press **⌘⇧L** and drag around a printed equation in a PDF or website to copy LaTeX. Pix2Text recognition and equation previews run on your Mac.
- Copy raw LaTeX, Markdown, or LaTeX delimiters, or set a custom prefix and suffix. Changing the format recopies the latest equation.
- Open **Equation History** to browse rendered copies, click to copy them again, or drag them into a compatible text field. History keeps 10 equations by default and supports up to 5,000. You can pause recording or clear saved entries in the History panel.
- Customize shortcuts, capture dimming, and Launch at Login in Settings.

Requires an Apple silicon Mac with macOS 14 or later. The app is ad-hoc signed and unnotarized. If macOS blocks the first launch, follow the [installation guide](https://github.com/exploringtruth/latexshot#if-macos-blocks-the-app).

Download [LaTeXShot.dmg](https://github.com/exploringtruth/latexshot/releases/download/v1.0.0/LaTeXShot.dmg) or the [ZIP](https://github.com/exploringtruth/latexshot/releases/download/v1.0.0/LaTeXShot-1.0.0.zip). Verify either download against [SHA256SUMS](https://github.com/exploringtruth/latexshot/releases/download/v1.0.0/SHA256SUMS). This build uses manual downloads for updates.

The frozen printed-equation benchmark accepted 60 of 66 results (90.9%), below the 95% target. Review the copied LaTeX before using it. [Benchmark results](https://github.com/exploringtruth/latexshot/blob/v1.0.0/benchmarks/pix2text-v1/README.md)
